structure: Part 2, journey flow, run, task rows and hub. Read in full the 17 files in the part's read list: journeys/linear/flow/flow.js (66 lines: 9 sections in page order, the review gate, FLOW_ONLY_KEYS, ordering rules in its doc comment), flow/run.js (59 lines: RUN_STEPS, the 9-step opening run, and nextRunTarget), flow/task-rows.js (46 lines: 7 task rows and rowStatus), flow/entry-guard.js (62 lines: the deep-link guard), flow/section-captions/index.js with copy.en.js and copy.cy.js (5 caption sections, the caption-free pages), features/index.js (17 route sets and 13 dispatch pages), features/evaluation.js (10 evaluation bindings), obligations/index.js (25 obligations, the obligation set index), the hub feature (controller.js, template.njk, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js: route, Overview heading, 4 numbered groups, 8 row titles, 5 status tags, Return to dashboard button), hub.fit.spec.js (12 tests), section-caption.fit.spec.js (2 tests) and routes-high-risk-plants.js (113 lines: the set's mount and the journey-flow seams it configures). To state how row status, row entry and Continue are worked out, also read the platform helpers these files call (shared/paths.js, bridge/status/index.js, flow/navigation.js, set.js); claims resting on those are marked inferred. Each section's own pages and obligation section files are left to the parts that own them. Claims run: flow order, opening run, task rows and status, entry guard, section captions, feature registry and obligation set, set mount, hub page, then the fit specs, then gaps.

claims.statement: The high-risk plants journey has 9 sections in this order: start, commodity, commodityDetails, origin, arrival, destination, parties, contact, review.
claims.quote:
export const sections = [
  { id: 'start', pages: [dashboardPage] },
  { id: 'commodity', pages: [commodityTypePage, commoditiesPage] },
  { id: 'commodityDetails', pages: [commodityDetailsPage] },
  { id: 'origin', pages: [originPage] },
  { id: 'arrival', pages: [arrivalStatusPage, arrivalDetailsPage] },
  { id: 'destination', pages: [placeOfDestinationPage] },
  { id: 'parties', pages: [consignorPage, identificationNumbersPage] },
  { id: 'contact', pages: [consignmentContactSelectPage] },

claims.statement: The start section holds only the dashboard page (the set's root, slug empty).
The commodity section asks the commodity type question (slug commodity-type) and then shows the commodities list page (slug commodities).

The commodity details sub-page (slug commodities/details) sits in a section of its own rather than after the list page; it is reached from the commodities list and returns to it, never by continuing past the list.
claims.quote:
The commodity entry sub-page sits in a section of its own rather than after
 * the list page it belongs to. `nextInSection` sends a page's Continue to the
 * next page in the same section, and the list page's Continue leaves the
 * commodity section altogether — the entry page is reached from the list and
 * returns to it, never by continuing past it.

claims.statement: The commodity details sub-page carries the commodity-type prerequisite: it cannot be reached until the commodity type is answered.
claims.quote:
Its own section still gives it
 * the commodity-type prerequisite that every page after the entry question
 * carries.

claims.statement: Every page after the commodity type entry question requires the commodity type to be answered before it can be reached.
claims.quote:
the commodity-type prerequisite that every page after the entry question
 * carries.

claims.statement: Origin comes after the commodity details sub-page; because the origin answer is enforced at Continue, every page after origin needs it, and placing it earlier would stop a trader adding a commodity line until they had named a country.
claims.quote:
Origin follows the entry sub-page rather than preceding it. Its answer is
 * enforced at Continue, so every page placed after it needs one; ahead of the
 * entry sub-page it would stop a trader adding a commodity line until they had
 * named a country.

claims.statement: The arrival section opens on the arrival status question, whose answer decides what the rest of the section asks, and goes on to the arrival details page.
claims.quote:
The arrival section opens on the arrival-status question, whose answer
 * decides what the rest of the section asks for, and goes on to the arrival
 * details.

claims.statement: Potato notifications are never asked the arrival status question: it is out of scope for them, so both the opening run and the arrival row's hub link skip it and land on arrival details, which every commodity type answers.
claims.quote:
Potato notifications never see the question: `arrivalStatus` is out
 * of scope for them, so the derived page gate fails and both the opening run
 * and the arrival row's hub entry (`rowGatePasses`/`rowEntry`) pass it over,
 * landing on arrival-details instead — a page every commodity type answers.

claims.statement: The place of destination page is its own section after the arrival section, so Continue on arrival details leaves the arrival section rather than running on into destination.

The place of destination page shows one of three questions depending on the arrival status; arrival status is not a prerequisite for it, and a trader entering from the hub with no status answered gets the pre-arrival question.
claims.quote:
so the page usually has a status to work from and
 * shows the right one of its three questions. It is not a prerequisite: a
 * trader entering from the hub with no status answered gets the pre-arrival
 * question, which is what the page falls back to.

claims.statement: The parties section asks for the consignor (slug consignors/select) and then the identification numbers (slug identification-numbers).
The contact section holds the consignment contact address page (slug consignment/contact/select) alone.
The review section runs check answers (slug notification-view), then the declaration, then the confirmation page.
The review section is gated: it cannot be entered until the notification is ready for check your answers.
The declaration is a flow-only key: it is held as session state rather than as a fulfilled notification answer, and it never counts as user progress.
Continue on a journey page goes to the next reachable page in the same section, and to the hub when the section has no further reachable page.
claims.quote:
`nextInSection` sends a page's Continue to the
 * next page in the same section
claims.note: The fall-back to the hub comes from the platform's nextInSection in flow/navigation.js (outside the set), which returns hubPath when no later page in the section passes its gate.

claims.statement: The opening run asks, in order: commodity type, commodities, origin, arrival status, arrival details, place of destination, consignor, identification numbers, consignment contact.

claims.statement: In the opening run, Continue on a step goes to the next step whose page the notification can reach; a step whose page is gated out is skipped.
claims.quote:
const flowPageTarget = (page) => (scope, journeyId) =>
  pageGatePasses(page, scope) ? pagePath(journeyId, page.slug) : null

claims.statement: When no later run step is reachable (including after the last step, consignment contact), the opening run's Continue goes to the notification's hub (task list).
The commodity details sub-page is not an opening run step: the commodities list sends a trader with no commodity lines there and takes them back to the list.
claims.quote:
The entry sub-page is not a step: the list page
 * sends a trader with no lines there and takes them back.

claims.statement: The opening run skips the arrival status step for potatoes.
claims.quote:
The
 * arrival-status step is skipped for potatoes, whose notification is never asked the
 * question.

claims.statement: The opening run asks arrival details and place of destination of every commodity type.
claims.quote: Arrival details and destination are asked of every commodity type;

claims.statement: The opening run skips the consignor step for potatoes, and every commodity type then reaches identification numbers.
claims.quote:
the consignor step is skipped for potatoes, then every type reaches

claims.statement: A page that is not an opening run step (such as commodity details or the review pages) gets no run target, so the run does not decide where its Continue goes.
claims.note: nextRunTarget returns null for a step id not in RUN_STEPS; what the caller does with null is the platform's (outside this part).

claims.statement: The hub has 7 task rows backed by journey pages, in this order: commodities, origin, arrival, destination, consignor, identification numbers, contact.
The commodities task row covers the commodity type, commodities list and commodity details pages.
The origin task row covers the origin page.
The arrival task row covers the arrival status and arrival details pages and is unconditional; for a potato notification it opens on the arrival details page.
claims.quote:
The arrival row holds the arrival question and the arrival details. The
 * question is out of scope for potatoes, so a potato notification opens the row
 * on the details page instead — every commodity type owes a date. The row is
 * not marked `conditional`: no notification finds the whole of it inapplicable.

claims.statement: The destination task row covers the place of destination page and is unconditional, because every commodity type owes a place of destination.
claims.quote:
The destination is a row of its own beside it in the same hub group. Every
 * commodity type owes a place of destination, so it too is unconditional.

claims.statement: The consignor task row is conditional: the hub hides it when the row does not apply to the notification at all (status not applicable), as for potatoes.
The identification numbers task row covers the identification numbers page.
The contact task row covers the consignment contact address page.
A task row's status is worked out from the answers its pages collect, giving one of five values: not applicable, not started, in progress, completed (fulfilled) or optional.
claims.quote:
export const rowParts = (row) =>
  row.parts ?? row.pages.flatMap((page) => collectsOf(page.id))

export const rowStatus = (row, answers, inScope, evaluation) =>
  statusOf(rowParts(row), answers, inScope, evaluation)

claims.statement: A task row is not applicable when none of the answers its pages collect is in scope for the notification.
claims.note: Read in the platform's bridge/status module (outside the set) to explain how task-rows.js rowStatus resolves.

claims.statement: A task row with required answers is completed when every required answer is satisfied, in progress when something is started but not all required answers are satisfied, and not started when nothing is started.
claims.note: Platform status module, read to explain task-rows.js rowStatus.

claims.statement: A task row with no required answers is optional while untouched, and once started is completed when every in-scope answer is satisfied and in progress otherwise.
claims.quote:
// No required parts: OPTIONAL if untouched, else FULFILLED/IN_PROGRESS by
// whether every in-scope part is satisfied.
claims.note: Platform status module, read to explain task-rows.js rowStatus.

claims.statement: A hub task row links to the first page in the row the notification can reach; a row is enterable when any of its pages is reachable, not only its first.
claims.note: rowEntry and rowGatePasses live in the platform's flow/navigation.js: 'Whether the hub can open a task row at all — true when any of its pages is reachable'.

claims.statement: A hub task row none of whose pages is reachable shows the status 'Cannot start yet' and has no link.
The entry guard applies to paths under the set's /notifications/ prefix that name a journey, but not to the create-notification path itself.
The entry guard does not apply to the notification action pages amend, cancel-amend, copy and delete.
The entry guard does not apply to the commodity type page or any path beneath it, the journey's entry surface.
The entry guard covers the hub (the notification's own path) as well as every journey page other than commodity type, since those paths name a journey and are not an action or the entry surface.
claims.note: The hub path /notifications/{journeyId} yields an empty slug, which is neither an action slug nor the entry surface, so it is guarded.

claims.statement: A deep link to a guarded journey path is redirected to that journey's commodity type page when the session holds no opening run record for the journey and the notification has no committed user answers.
claims.quote:
/** Deep-link guard: a journey with neither a run record in this session nor
 * committed user answers is sent to the entry page

claims.statement: Only an answer the user entered counts as starting a journey for the entry guard; system-populated obligations and flow-only keys such as the declaration do not.
claims.quote:
/** Only a model answer the USER entered starts a journey. System populated
 * obligations do not represent user progress, and flow-only keys such as
 * `declaration` are session state rather than canonical fulfilment, so they
 * never resolve to a manifest obligation. */

At start-up the set checks that its obligations are pure and that every obligation has a fulfilment binding.
